spudded_on: The subject well was spudded (drilling started) on the object date.
reached_td: The subject well reached its total depth (TD) at the object depth.
drilled_to: The subject well was drilled to the object depth (an intermediate or section depth, including "section TD").
set_casing_at: The subject casing, liner or conductor was set, landed or run to the object depth (shoe or setting depth).
casing_size: The subject tubular has the object outside diameter.
casing_spec: The subject tubular has the object weight and/or grade (e.g. "23 lb/ft P-110").
cemented_interval: Cement was placed behind or in the subject over the object interval, or its top of cement (TOC) is at the object depth.
set_plug_at: The subject plug was set or placed at the object depth or over the object interval.
set_equipment_at: The subject packer, nipple, valve, tubing stop, hanger or retainer was set or is located at the object depth.
tagged_at: A tool tagged the subject (plug, TOC, fill, fish, obstruction) at the object depth.
cut_at: The subject was cut (and possibly pulled) at the object depth (often BML).
tested_to_pressure: The subject was pressure-tested to the object pressure.
fit_lot_emw: A formation integrity or leak-off test of the subject well held the object equivalent mud weight.
perforated_interval: The subject (well, tubing string, or zone) was perforated over the object interval.
has_mud_weight: The subject well's mud/fluid weight was (raised, reduced or displaced) to the object density.
completed_in: The subject well was completed or recompleted in the object zone.
encountered_marker: The subject well encountered (logged, penetrated) the object geologic marker or formation.
has_well_status: The subject well has or entered the object status (TA, PA, COM, ST, BP, SI).
used_rig: Operations on the subject well used the object rig or vessel.
operated_by: The subject well is operated by the object company (stated as operator, not a service company).
pumped: The object volume of the subject fluid was pumped or mixed and pumped.
